Detailed information on K2CO3 activation 
During the activation process, K 2CO3 decomposes into CO 2 and K 2O, which reacts with C 
atoms and then generates K and CO. When the temperature exceeds the boiling point of K 
(about 800 °C), the K vapor drills into the carbon layer and causes damage to the structure of 
the carbon material. In addition, the CO 2 produced during the activation process also plays a 
physical porosity role on the carbon structure [40].
